worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-3,$ ${x}_{2}=2,$ and ${x}_{3,4}=-1\pm \text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=3.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) \\  & =3(x-(-3))(x-2)(x-(-1+\text{i}))(x-(-1-\text{i})) \\  & =3(x+3)(x-2)(x-(-1+\text{i}))(x-(-1-\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3(x+3)(x-2)(x-(-1+\text{i}))(x-(-1-\text{i})) & = \\ 3({x}^{2}-2x+3x-6)({x}^{2}-x(-1-\text{i})-x(-1+\text{i})+(-1+\text{i})(-1-\text{i})) & = \\ 3({x}^{2}+x-6)\,({x}^{2}+2x+2) & = \\ 3({x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+2x-6{x}^{2}-12x-12) & = \\ 3({x}^{4}+3{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-10x-12) & = \\ 3{x}^{4}+9{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}-30x-36 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=3{x}^{4}+9{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}-30x-36.$

EXPLANATION

From the diagram, we see that f(x) has roots x1=−3, x2=2, and x3,4=−1±i. Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the quartic term is a=3. Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

f(x)=a(x−x1)(x−x2)(x−x3)(x−x4)=3(x−(−3))(x−2)(x−(−1+i))(x−(−1−i))=3(x+3)(x−2)(x−(−1+i))(x−(−1−i))

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain 3(x+3)(x−2)(x−(−1+i))(x−(−1−i))=3(x2−2x+3x−6)(x2−x(−1−i)−x(−1+i)+(−1+i)(−1−i))=3(x2+x−6)(x2+2x+2)=3(x4+2x3+2x2+x3+2x2+2x−6x2−12x−12)=3(x4+3x3−2x2−10x−12)=3x4+9x3−6x2−30x−36.

Therefore, f(x)=3x4+9x3−6x2−30x−36.
